qualifying.hardware_type: Five on-site gas turbine generators on Barrow Island generating up to 584 MW combined at full output, powering the Gorgon LNG/domestic-gas processing complex -- Chevron Australia's managing director described the output as comparable in scale to the Kwinana power station supplying greater Perth, consistent with heavy-duty industrial frame-class turbines.

qualifying.basis: Qualifies both ways: individual >=50 MW (heavy-duty single units, ~117 MW each) and aggregate >=50 MW (584 MW total). No material judgment call -- both figures clear the threshold comfortably.

qualifying.hardware_type: 12x GE LM6000PF aero-derivative gas turbines (6 per LNG train, 2 trains) in pure mechanical-drive service, directly shaft-driving the ConocoPhillips Optimized Cascade refrigeration compressors with no electricity generated -- the first industrial application of the LM6000PF; Train 2 was later upgraded to the higher-output LM6000PF+.
qualifying.individual_mw: ~45-50 MW shaft each (LM6000PF class rating; Train 2 upgraded to the higher-output LM6000PF+; no site-specific figure published)
qualifying.basis: Aggregate >=50 MW (aeroderivative rule; mechanical drive) -- 12 LM6000PF aeroderivative units aggregate far past the threshold regardless of where the individual unit falls in the ~45-50 MW class range. (Individually the PF/PF+ variant sits at/near 50 MW -- borderline, so the aggregate is the qualifying basis.)

qualifying.status: operating; cancelled (unspecified expansion/component only -- the terminal-level facility remains active and operating, so it is not excluded on status)
qualifying.hardware_type: Multiple aero-derivative gas turbine generators (one held in standby) provide the plant's primary electrical power per PNG LNG's Environmental Impact Statement (Chapter 4, a primary regulatory filing), sized for a base load of 44,267 kW (LNG trains + storage + utilities + offsites + camps) with a design capacity up to 59,760 kW (20% growth + 15% contingency margin). Separately, aero-derivative gas turbines shaft-drive the refrigerant/liquefaction compressors (mechanical drive, no electricity generated). Diesel-engine generators are separate/non-gas, essential/black-start only, and out of scope.
qualifying.aggregate_mw: 44.267 MW current base load; design-sized generation capacity up to 59.76 MW
qualifying.basis: Aggregate >=50 MW (aeroderivative/genset rule) -- JUDGMENT CALL: qualification uses the EIS's design-sized generation capacity (~59.8 MW, built in to accommodate 20% growth + 15% contingency) rather than the 44.267 MW current base load, which alone would fall short of the 50 MW threshold. Flag for review. Separately-documented mechanical-drive turbines shaft-driving the compressors are not MW-quantified and are not needed to reach the qualifying call.
